_doc: Where a reader marked the STAND-IN's facial landmarks (a house maid in a 1908 General Electric advertising photograph, not Mary Reynolds), in pixels of the crop `crop_px` of the Library of Congress master. Her face is near frontal, turned a little to her right, so her LEFT ear (the reader's right) is marked. She smiles broadly with her lips parted: the stomion is the middle of the open mouth and carries a wide uncertainty, and the smile widens and lifts the lower face. The scan is soft at this size. `base_body` fits against Mary Reynolds's own body's rest face.
age_note: The stand-in is unnamed and her age is not recorded; she looks to be in her twenties, so 25 is a reading of the picture. The renderer's ageing pair takes the face to Mary Reynolds's own 33 at the scene date.
basis: No photograph of Mary Reynolds is known. Her face's proportions are fitted to a stand-in: an unnamed American house maid in cap and apron in a 1908 photograph (Library of Congress, LC-USZ62-67635), a woman of about her age, place and work. It is not her: what the face shows is that kind of woman, not Mary Reynolds, so the face is reconstructed.
not_modelled: her own face (no photograph of her is known; this is a stand-in's)
her hair (the stand-in's is drawn up under a cap; the model wears the town's bun)
